class_weighting: NONE_UNWEIGHTED_BCE remains frozen unless an owner decision changes it; a probabilistic target uses the same unweighted principle
frozen_reduction: average equally over COMPACT/LINE and robots within a decision, then over decision events

numeric_demonstration.note: R changes the observation k/R, not the weight

principle: each (source event, candidate) remains ONE scientific unit regardless of R and regardless of team size

required_normalization_for_a_binomial_ta.net_effect: every retained decision event contributes weight 1.0
required_normalization_for_a_binomial_ta.per_event_term: average the two candidate terms (weight 0.5 each)
required_normalization_for_a_binomial_ta.per_robot_term: average over the N robot-local rows within one (event, candidate) before the candidate average, preserving the existing frozen reduction
required_normalization_for_a_binomial_ta.why_divide_by_R: this is the MEAN per-replica negative log likelihood, which is invariant to R. Without the 1/R factor an R = 9 event would contribute nine times the gradient of an R = 1 event.

what_would_go_wrong_without_it: F8 and F9 are the only multi-replica families. Weighting by replica count would silently up-weight exactly the two stochastic families and bias the model toward them, which is the opposite of the frozen uniform family budget
